Last weekend, I ordered dinner through a delivery app, and I was starving by the time it was supposed to arrive.
I kept checking my phone every five minutes, watching the little map, waiting for the driver to show up and my food to finally get there.
Finally, someone knocked, and I grabbed the bag without even really looking at it.
I was that hungry.
I sat down, opened it up, and immediately knew something was wrong.
I had ordered noodles.
This bag had, like, three burgers and a huge box of fries, none of which I remembered ordering.
I checked the receipt stapled to the bag, and sure enough, it had someone else's name on it.
Not mine.
So somewhere out there, someone was probably opening a bag of noodles right now, just as confused as I was, staring at food they never ordered.
I called the restaurant, and the guy who picked up sounded a little panicked, like this had happened before and he really didn't want it to happen again on his shift.
He asked me to hang on to the burgers and said he'd send the driver back to fix everything as soon as possible.
While I waited, I mean, I wasn't just going to let good fries go cold, right?
So I ate a few.
Just to be polite to the driver, obviously, not because I was starving.
That's what I told myself, anyway, while reaching for a third one.
About twenty minutes later, the same driver showed up again, looking pretty stressed out and a little out of breath.
He apologized like five times, handed me the correct bag of noodles, and took back what was left of the burgers, which, honestly, wasn't much at that point.

He explained that he'd delivered to the wrong building because two streets nearby have almost the exact same name, and it gets mixed up all the time, apparently more often than the app would like to admit.
Apparently I wasn't even the first mix-up that night, and he sounded genuinely exhausted just talking about it.
He also mentioned that the app had already flagged the address as a common problem spot, but nobody had gotten around to fixing it yet.
I told him that honestly, at least the food had been good, wrong order or not, and he actually laughed for the first time since he'd shown up.
The restaurant ended up giving me a discount on my next order for the trouble, which I definitely wasn't expecting.
So in the end, I got noodles, a few free fries, and a good story to tell later.
Honestly, not the worst way a wrong order could've gone.
